name: Penile girth and length surgery

lead: Penile enlargement surgery is cosmetic surgery intended to increase the length or girth of the penis. Lengthening usually means releasing the suspensory ligament; girth is addressed with fat or dermal-fat grafts or injectable fillers.

People seek it to change how their body looks and feels about it. It has been called the second most desired cosmetic procedure in men by a 2023 plastic-surgery paper, and medical bodies are cautious about it.

paras: Procedures are performed by surgeons in clinics. Lengthening procedures are often combined with a grafted or injected girth procedure, and traction weights have been used afterwards in older descriptions.

Reported complications include scarring, lumps, deformity, loss of grafted fat and sexual-function problems. The American Urological Association has stated that fat injection and ligament division are not shown to be safe or effective, and permanent fillers are advised against by the Sexual Medicine Society of North America [1].

angle.text: Men consider these procedures to change how the penis looks. Professional bodies report limited and variable results, and the motivations studied are largely psychological and social.

lead: Penile girth and length surgery refers to cosmetic procedures aimed at enlarging the penis. The main options are suspensory ligament release for length, and fat injection, dermal-fat grafting or fillers for girth [1][2]. A 2023 anatomical study describes enlargement surgery as the second most desired cosmetic procedure in men worldwide, with ligament release as the mainstay of lengthening [3].

Ligament release can lengthen the flaccid penis but not the erect penis and may affect sexual function, according to a Wikipedia summary [1]. In the 1990s, surgeons reported reconstructing deformities after enlargement performed elsewhere, including hypertrophic scars, penile lumps and nodules, and fat disappearance [4].

The American Urological Association states fat injection and ligament division have not been shown to be safe or effective, and a 2019 review reported poor outcomes with low satisfaction [1]. A 2026 qualitative study found motivations differ: heterosexual men emphasised partner-related pressures, while gay men emphasised community and body-image influences [5]. Surgery is medically indicated for micropenis [1].
infobox: Fillers not FDA approved for the penis

paras: Aesthetic penile surgery covers the penis, scrotum and pubic region. Lengthening has been performed by releasing the suspensory ligament, followed in older practice by penile weights, and girth by wrapping a dermal-fat graft [2].
Patients and some clinics present the surgery as improving body image and satisfaction. Professional reviews describe low satisfaction and significant risk of major complications [1].

A cadaver and clinical study found that sectioning the fundiform and suspensory ligaments did not destabilise the penis, and described cautious release as a way to lengthen [3]. A 2008 review discusses indications, procedures and complications for length, girth and skin reconstruction [6]. Some doctors say most men seeking enlargement are of normal size, and penile dysmorphophobia has been described [1].

Reported problems include wide scars, a proximal penile hump from a hair-bearing flap, a low-hanging penis, vanishing fat, lumps and shaft deformities [4]. Injectables carry swelling, deformity and, in severe cases, removal; unlicensed practitioners in Vietnam in 2013 left men hospitalised with infection and necrosis after silicone injection [1].

Published work includes case series, reviews and a 2023 study of 30 micropenis patients operated with ligament release and lipofilling [3]. A 2019 review summarised results as poor with low satisfaction [1].
